arxiv-2102-04808.title: Smart non-intrusive appliance identification using a novel local power histogramming descriptor with an improved k-nearest neighbors classifier
arxiv-2102-04808.creator: Yassine Himeur, Abdullah Alsalemi, Faycal Bensaali, Abbes Amira
arxiv-2102-04808.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yassine Himeur, Abdullah Alsalemi, Faycal Bensaali, Abbes Amira. Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) is a key cost-effective technology for monitoring power consumption and contributing to several challenges encountered when transiting to an efficient, sustainable, and competitive energy efficiency environment. This paper proposes a smart NILM system based on a novel local power histogramming (LPH) descriptor, in which appliance power signals are transformed into 2D space and short histograms are extracted to represent each device.

arxiv-2410-17952.title: SimRAG: Self-Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Adapting Large Language Models to Specialized Domains
arxiv-2410-17952.creator: Ran Xu, Hui Liu, Sreyashi Nag, Zhenwei Dai, Yaochen Xie, Xianfeng Tang, Chen Luo, Yang Li, Joyce C. Ho, Carl Yang, Qi He, Emory University Amazon {ran.xu,joyce.c.ho,j.carlyang}@emory.edu , liunhu@amazon.com
arxiv-2410-17952.description: Abstract Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances the question answering (QA) abilities of large language models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge. However, adapting general-purpose RAG systems to specialized fields such as science and medicine poses unique challenges due to distribution shifts and limited access to domain-specific data.

arxiv-2502-12289.title: Evaluating Step-by-step Reasoning Traces: A Survey
arxiv-2502-12289.creator: Jinu Lee, Julia Hockenmaier
arxiv-2502-12289.description: Abstract Step-by-step reasoning is widely used to enhance the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs) in complex problems. Evaluating the quality of reasoning traces is crucial for understanding and improving LLM reasoning. However, existing evaluation practices are highly inconsistent, resulting in fragmented progress across evaluator design and benchmark development.

arxiv-2510-26687.title: The ODYSSEUS Survey. Spatial correlation of magnetospheric inclinations points to parsec-scale star-cloud connection Journal: ApJL Facilities: VLT:Antu, VLT:Kueyen, VLT:Melipal, VLT:Yepun (ESPRESSO, UVES, X-Shooter), CTIO:1.5m astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al
arxiv-2510-26687.creator: Caeley V. Pittman, Catherine C. Espaillat, Thanawuth Thanathibodee, Nuria Calvet, Lee W. Hartmann, Sylvie Cabrit
arxiv-2510-26687.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Caeley V. Pittman, Catherine C. Espaillat, Thanawuth Thanathibodee, Nuria Calvet, Lee W. Hartmann, Sylvie Cabrit. The properties of stars and planets are shaped by the initial conditions of their natal clouds. However, the spatial scales over which the initial conditions can exert a significant influence are not well constrained. We report the first evidence for parsec-scale spatial correlations of stellar magnetospheric inclinations ( i mag i_{\rm mag} ), observed in the Lupus low-mass star forming region.

arxiv-2601-00808.title: Implementation of the Spherical Trigonometry Algorithm in a Qibla Direction Application
arxiv-2601-00808.creator: 1 st Wisnu Uriawan, 2 nd Andika Nuralamsyah, 3 rd Abidzar Giffari, 4 th Arief Rahman Mubarok, 5 th Aisyah Muthmainnah, 6 th Najwa Naura Salsabilla Herdiyana
arxiv-2601-00808.description: Abstract This research explores the implementation of a spherical trigonometry algorithm in the development of QiblatKita, a mobile-based Qibla direction application designed to address the need for accurate and accessible prayer direction tools for Muslims, especially in the context of global mobility and diverse geographical settings.

pmc-10737916.title: EXAMINING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN HYDRATION STATUS AND OBESITY IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10737916.creator: Kworweinski Lafontant, Ladda Thiamwong, Jeffery Stout, Joon-Hyuk Park, Rui Xie, David Fukuda
pmc-10737916.description: Adequate hydration is an important modifiable determinant of overall physical health within community-dwelling older adults. Research and clinical practice often use urine osmolarity and bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) to assess hydration status. Prior evidence links inadequate hydration to increased obesity, typically measured by body mass index (BMI).

pmc-11591410.title: Applications, Limitations, and Considerations of Clinical Trials in a Dish
pmc-11591410.creator: Amatullah Mir, Angie Zhu, Rico Lau, Nicolás Barr, Zyva Sheikh, Diana Acuna, Anuhya Dayal, Narutoshi Hibino
pmc-11591410.description: Recent advancements in biotechnology forged the path for clinical trials in dish (CTiDs) to advance as a popular method of experimentation in biomedicine. CTiDs play a fundamental role in translational research through technologies such as induced pluripotent stem cells, whole genome sequencing, and organs-on-a-chip.

pmc-12358504.title: Association between Ki-67 and clinical outcomes in 324 Chinese patients with resectable acral melanoma
pmc-12358504.creator: Yi Teng, Jin Wu, Weizhen Zhang, Kui Jiang, Xin Cai, Jianping Gui, Hongfeng Zhou, Yan Wang, Fang Liu, Jiwei Liu, Zhen Guo, Hongxue Meng, Mei Xiang, Xiang Ji, Di Wu
pmc-12358504.description: The relationship between Ki-67 expression and clinical prognosis in patients with resectable acral melanoma (AM) remains unclear. This study explores the prognostic role of Ki-67 in AM using data from 324 patients across five Chinese centers. Patients were divided into low Ki-67 expression and high Ki-67 expression groups based on pathological reports.

pmc-12615878.title: How skin achieves mechano-resistance for land movement: the critical role of ER sensing
pmc-12615878.creator: Weihong Fu, Hua Li, Wenxiu Ning
pmc-12615878.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To adapt to gravitational forces during the transition to terrestrial life, animals evolved specialized paw skin to withstand their body weight and allow for locomotion. In a recent Cell article, Di et al. demonstrate SLURP1 as an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane protein that protects palmoplantar keratinocytes from mechanical stress by preserving SERCA2b activity and inhibiting the pPERK-NRF2 signaling under mechanical pressure.

pmc-13353553.title: Triggers, Responses, and Outcomes for Patient Related Violence and/or Aggression Events During Acute Hospitalisation: A Documentary Analysis
pmc-13353553.creator: Debra Kerr, Alison M Hutchinson, Elisa Ilarda, Louise Alexander, Susan Perlen, Nicole Davies, Trish Mant, Angela Skazlic, Joanna Petrunic, Rachel Mrhar, Adam Searby
pmc-13353553.description: AimTo examine triggers, responses, and outcomes for patient‐related violence and/or aggression events during acute hospitalisation.DesignThis was a descriptive observational study undertaken at two healthcare organisations.MethodsPre‐existing data were extracted from organisational incident reports and individual medical records during a retrospective period (1/1/2023 to 30/6/2023) and a prospective period (7/6/2024 to 16/11/2024).

pmc-13469672.title: Research on a fast self-healing control method for tie-line faults in regional distribution networks based on source–load–storage interaction
pmc-13469672.creator: Chuan Zhou, Suying Gui, Guomin Gao, Chaoyi Liu, Yongtao Ma
pmc-13469672.description: To address the challenges of islanding susceptibility, complex network topology, and insufficient coordination between traditional protection and stability control under high penetration of distributed generation in regional distribution networks, a fast fault self-healing control method based on source–load–storage coordinated interaction is proposed.

pmc-13675208.title: Constructing melanopic light exposure profiles from sparse daily-route measurements
pmc-13675208.creator: Niloufar Tabandeh, Jennifer A Veitch, Manuel Spitschan
pmc-13675208.description: Daily light exposure is temporally structured, yet calibrated spectral measurements are usually available only at selected locations and times. Turning such a sparse library into a schedule-resolved profile requires an assignment rule: a decision about which measurements may represent each unmeasured part of the day. We examined how much that decision matters.

uslaw-usc-t25-s352a.title: 25 U.S.C. § 352a — Cancellation of patents in fee simple for allotments held in trust
uslaw-usc-t25-s352a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s352a.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 9 (Allotment Of Indian Lands). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized, in his discretion, to cancel any patent in fee simple issued to an Indian allottee or to his heirs before the end of the period of trust described in the original or trust patent issued to such allottee.

uslaw-usc-t42-s238c.title: 42 U.S.C. § 238c — Transportation of remains of officers
uslaw-usc-t42-s238c.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s238c.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 6A (Public Health Service); Subchapter I (Administration And Miscellaneous Provisions); Part B (Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Appropriations available for traveling expenses of the Service shall be available for meeting the cost of preparation for burial and of transportation to the place of burial of remains of commissioned officers.
